Project: Space Observation Project 1, Group 2
Lecturer: Dr. Nguyen Thi Phuong
USTH, Master 2 Space, 25 November 2026
1  Introduction. What? One question, three checks
From a raw TESS light curve, how closely can we recover a planet's orbital period and radius, and for which kinds of planet does it fail?
Period
All ten periods agree with the NASA Exoplanet Archive to 0.03 % or better.
Radius
Eight of ten radii agree within 4 %; the largest gap is 7.3 % (K2-141 b). Every gap is within 1.4σ.
Coverage
Ten planets from 1.1 to 15.7 R⊕ and 0.28 to 6.1 d, plus two stress tests that fail.
We measure; the catalog is only the answer key. A radius needs the stellar radius, which does not come from the light curve.

4  Discussion. Where the method fails: three lessons
Blind search can lock on noise
K2-141 b: blind BLS gave 5.70 d instead of 0.280 d. The browser demo returns 2×P for LTT 1445 A b. Narrow the range (5 to 6 d, or 0.26 to 0.5 d) and both are fixed.
Active stars break detrending
AU Mic b (spots, flares): R<sub>p</sub>/R<sub>★</sub> = 0.25 ± 0.11 against 0.050. DS Tuc A b: systematic error ±0.12.
Few transits cap the accuracy
AU Mic b has 3 transits in one sector, with timing variations; LTT 1445 A b only 4. More sectors would help.
AU Mic b and DS Tuc A b are reported as failures and are not among the ten.

5  Conclusions and perspectives
What we showed
Periods of ten planets (0.28 to 6.1 d) within 0.03 % and radii (1.1 to 15.7 R<sub>⊕</sub>) within 4 % for eight of ten, from public data and one pipeline.
What limits it
Stellar radius (up to 7 %), detrending (about 1 %), the number of transits, and blind search at short periods or low S/N.
Next
Fit stellar density and eccentricity, search for TTVs, stack more sectors, Gaussian-process detrending for active stars.
A radius from a light curve is a ratio times a stellar radius; the ratio is the part TESS measures best.

These three formulas are the course formulas on transits (lecture review, section C). Example from the review: depth 0.64 %, R star 0.8 solar radii gives Rp/R star 0.08 and Rp 0.064 solar radii. Our pipeline does this fit properly, with limb darkening and MCMC, instead of reading the depth by eye.

Funnel. Tmag below 11 keeps the noise low, P below 15 days gives two or more transits in one sector, and the estimated S over N above 12 uses a simple noise model. Ten plus two: ten representatives and two stress-test planets.

Size, orbit, star, distance, sky position and system type. The sky axis matters for TESS: the continuous viewing zone near the ecliptic poles is observed for about a year, low latitudes for one or two sectors.

Systematic error is half the range of Rp over R star across three detrending variants. For bright stars the MCMC error is below half a percent; the stellar radius is 1 to 7 percent. LTT 9779 b and K2-141 b are limited by the dip itself.

Be honest here. Guided mode is not cheating: it restricts the search window, the period and radius are still measured from the data, and every planet slide says which mode was used. Next step for active stars: Gaussian-process detrending, as in the stellar-variability tutorial.
